title: AppLovin vs. Reddit: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
AppLovin vs. Reddit: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Jake Lerch, The Motley Fool
Tue, October 13, 2026 at 9:35 AM MDT 7 min read
APP
RDDT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Digital advertising is evolving rapidly as automation and community engagement take center stage. Choosing between AppLovin (NASDAQ:APP) and Reddit (NYSE:RDDT)requires examining how each captures value in this shifting landscape.

AppLovin provides the technical backbone for mobile app monetization, while Reddit operates a vast network of interest-based communities. Both companies have achieved profitability and exhibit rapid revenue growth, making them key candidates for investors evaluating high-growth platforms in the digital advertising space. Their distinct business models offer different ways to play the internet software market.

The case for AppLovin

AppLovin sells marketing software and advertising solutions to mobile app developers and consumer brands. Its platform includes tools like Axon Ads Manager for user acquisition, MAX for in-app bidding, and Adjust for analytics. In its latest annual report, filed for the period ending Dec. 31, 2024, the company stated it had 1,563 employees across 17 countries and highlighted its focus on advertising technology among tech stocks that support the global mobile economy. By divesting its apps business, the company now concentrates entirely on its software platform.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $5.5 billion, representing a significant 70% increase over the $3.2 billion reported in the previous year. The company reported net income of roughly $3.3 billion during this period, which is more than double its FY 2024 performance. This expansion yielded an impressive net margin of approximately 60.8%, demonstrating its ability to translate higher sales into earnings while maintaining low operating costs relative to its scale.

The company maintains a current ratio of about 3.3x, which indicates its ability to cover short-term liabilities with assets such as cash. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, its debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 1.7x, a measure of total debt relative to shareholders' equity. Free cash flow for the year reached close to $3.9 billion, representing cash from operations after subtracting capital expenditures. This strong cash generation provides the company with significant flexibility for future investments or debt reduction.

The case for Reddit

Reddit operates a community platform where users discuss interests across thousands of distinct forums, providing a unique environment for advertisers. It generates revenue primarily from third-party advertising, which accounted for approximately 94% of its revenue in FY 2025. While revenue is significantly concentrated among a small number of top advertisers, the company is now exploring additional streams, such as content licensing for artificial intelligence training and developer programs. This strategy aims to monetize the vast amount of user-generated content hosted on the site.

Meta Platforms META shares have rallied 12.4% in the past three-month period, outperforming the broader Zacks Computer & Technology sector's return of 5.8%.

The company's shares have also outperformed its peers, which include Reddit RDDT, Amazon AMZN and Alphabet GOOGL. All three companies are expanding their footprints in the advertising space. While Reddit and Alphabet shares have lost 21.3% and 1.9%, respectively, Amazon shares have risen 4.9% in the past three-month period.

The outperformance can be attributed to robust advertising demand, AI-driven improvements in ad targeting and content recommendations, and growing user engagement across Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. Expanding adoption of Advantage+ advertising solutions and AI-powered creative tools is further supporting growth. The launch of Muse also remains a key catalyst. These factors are helping Meta Platforms fend off its competitors like Reddit, Amazon and Alphabet.

META Stock Performance
Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

META Benefits From Strong AI-Led Ad Performance

Meta Platforms' strong growth in the advertising business has been noteworthy. The company's focus on integrating AI into its platforms — Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger and Threads — is driving user and advertising engagement. In the second quarter of 2026, Meta Platforms reported $59.4 billion in ad revenues, up 27% year over year, with a 14% increase in ad impressions and a 12% rise in average price per ad.

AI is heavily dependent on data, of which META has a trove, driven by its more than 3.6 billion daily users. Instagram reached 2 billion daily active users and Threads surpassed 500 million monthly active users in the second quarter of 2026. AI-powered recommendation and ranking systems are also strengthening engagement across META's platforms. Instagram time spent grew double digits year over year, while Facebook video time spent increased 9% globally. Meta Platforms is using large language models (LLMs) to better understand content and user preferences, enabling more personalized recommendations across Feed and Reels.

In the second quarter of 2026, the deployment of Meta Generative Recommender and other advanced models led to an 8.3% increase in ad clicks and a 15.7% uplift in conversions on Facebook. More than 9 million small businesses now use at least one of Meta Platforms' AI-powered ad creative tools. Early LLM-powered initiatives also drove a 1% increase in app event conversions on Instagram. Its Advantage+ AI-powered advertising solutions also surpassed a $75 billion annual revenue run rate in the second quarter of 2026, highlighting growing advertiser adoption.

title: Is Reddit Stock a Good Fit For Your Portfolio Risk?
detail:
Is Reddit Stock a Good Fit For Your Portfolio Risk?
Trefis Team
Mon, October 12, 2026 at 4:28 PM MDT 4 min read

^GSPC
META

PINS
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Reddit (RDDT) has been listed for only 2.5 years, leaving investors with a short track record to evaluate. Most shareholders likely hold the stock alongside standard index funds that already track broader market movements. So when the market has a good day or a bad one, what does Reddit do to the rest of your money?

Reddit Goes Further Than Your Funds, Both Ways

On average, Reddit moves in the same direction as the broader market, but with wider swings that compound the market risk you already have. Over the past year of daily closes, the S&P 500 gained 0.65% on its average up day. On those days, a $10,000 investment in Reddit stock ended up worth about $10,130. Conversely, the index lost 0.6% on its average down day. That same $10,000 in Reddit ended those negative sessions worth about $9,850.

The stock amplifies market movements in both directions, though the losses on bad days outpace the gains on good ones. Specifically, the shares rose twice as far as the index on the up days and fell about two and a half times as far on the down days.

Two other metrics from the past year illustrate a similar pattern. Reddit's volatility, which measures the spread of its daily movements, sat at 70% a year compared to 13.0% for the S&P 500. Additionally, for each 1% the index moved, Reddit moved about 2% on average.

Has Reddit Rewarded You Well Enough?

The answer is only partly yes, based on the whole period since Reddit listed. Over that stretch, Reddit returned 56% a year, far outpacing the roughly 17% a year logged by the S&P 500. Shareholders earned more than the market, but they absorbed significant turbulence to achieve those gains. Reddit's volatility since it listed reached 81% a year, well above the 15.5% for the index.

Dividing each return by its volatility reveals the payoff for each unit of swing: 0.69 for Reddit since it listed, compared to about 1.1 for the S&P 500. This means Reddit compensates investors less efficiently for the turbulence they endure, even though the stock ultimately delivered higher raw returns.

Can Reddit's Business Calm The Stock Down?

Recent financial results provide little indication that the stock will stabilize. The company's reports point to continued swings matching the past year's pattern. Advertising revenue accounted for $762 million of the $805 million Reddit generated during the second quarter of 2026. This leaves the company with nearly all of its sales coming from a single line of business, though those sales are expanding rapidly. Total revenue rose 61% from a year earlier.

title: Is Meta's Next Big Thing Already Here?
detail:
Is Meta's Next Big Thing Already Here?

Image from Pixabay

Meta Platforms (META) stock returned 10.4% over the past month, outperforming the 1.8% return for the S&P 500. Investors have been optimistic about the company following the release of a new app on September 8, 2026. Nearly all of Meta's revenue still comes from ads, but this recent launch may signal the start of a broader business model. So what did Meta launch, and how far has it gotten?

Meta Launched Muse, A Personal AI Agent

Muse is an application designed to handle delegated tasks, such as booking travel and managing emails. It can also scan retail sites, locate specific products, and prepare a purchase for the user to approve. Meta has announced shopping partnerships with Walmart, Gap, Sephora and others.

Early adoption has already outpaced ChatGPT's initial rollout. Following its release, Muse topped OpenAI's ChatGPT in Apple iOS downloads. The app-analytics firm Apptopia estimated that Muse had 642,000 daily active users in the U.S. during its first twelve days. By comparison, Apptopia put ChatGPT at 231,000 daily active users at the same stage of its own mobile launch.

Executives signaled this strategic direction well before the release. During the company's second-quarter 2026 call in July, management stated that personal agents would serve as the foundation for its next wave of products and revenue lines. Meta offers a basic tier of Muse for free alongside paid subscription plans ($20 and $100 per month), while testing additional commercial monetization avenues such as transaction fees.

How Much Of Meta's Revenue Comes From Ads?

Ads brought in about 98% of Meta's revenue in the second quarter of 2026. That segment generated $59.4 billion out of a total $60.8 billion, meaning any new business would start small alongside the core advertising operations.

Yet there are signs of diversification. Within Meta's apps, revenue other than ads grew 73% from a year earlier, outpacing the 28% growth for the company as a whole. Management noted that this growth came mainly from WhatsApp paid messaging and subscriptions. Meta has therefore shown it can grow sales outside ads, even if its apps are building from a base of $1 billion in the quarter.

Muse could become the next source of non-ad revenue. According to an October 8, 2026 report by Proactive Investors, Meta hopes to monetize the app by collecting a percentage of each purchase that an agent makes for a consumer.

Even after the past month's gain, Meta stock remains 7.3% below its 52-week high. The shares have returned 1.4% over the past twelve months, trailing the 17.0% return for the S&P 500. Based on these figures, the current market price does not appear to factor in a large new business just yet.
